program: Free loans of reused durable medical equipment for adults and children

nutshell.headline: Low-cost equipment access is plausible; this model does not support a high-impact giving recommendation.
nutshell.body: A $10,000 gift by check to the whole organization produces 0.03322629 signed prior-weighted Bay QALYs, or $3,009,665 per 10. Central: $1,725,534. The favorable scenario receives a 3% subjective probability weight and contributes 91.8% of expected net Bay benefit. Utility, duration and additionality are judgments, not measured effects.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Volunteers repair, clean and lend donated equipment, potentially bridging unmet mobility and self-care needs.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Current public support, historical cash reserves, a forecast denominator and unvalidated utility transfer leave substantial null or harm risk.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Verify a small priced cash-triggered expansion or service-preservation plan, current reserve restrictions, unique recipients, device-class mix and actual use before recommending a gift.

summary.label: SOCIETAL COST
summary.detail: donated equipment, labor and travel not fully priced

programSection.body: MELP lends standard adult mobility and safety equipment; AbleCloset handles specialized pediatric equipment. Both are within EIN 27-1212734. Free loans are available from San Carlos and South San Francisco, without a residence restriction.

steps.title: Receive and prepare equipment
steps.detail: Volunteers inspect, repair, clean and inventory donations; not every incoming item is usable locally.

steps.title: Match a recipient
steps.detail: Inventory is first-come and users arrange pickup. Multiple items or visits need not mean multiple people.

steps.title: Enable finite additional use
steps.detail: Only otherwise-unmet, sustained safe health-improving use is credited; utility losses are subtracted separately.

programSection.boundary: Use planned whole-organization $169,269 expense and inferred 3,429 planning client-equivalents from 960/.28. The resulting $49.37 unit cost is not a historical actual or a funded marginal offer. Full 2024 expense of $104,000 is disclosed but not paired with newer output forecasts.

model.headline: Signed expected Bay cost: $3,009,665 per 10 QALYs
model.body: Calculate each joint scenario independently, subtract harms, then average QALYs using weights locked before execution. Divide the whole gift by expected net QALYs; do not average cost ratios or discard negative worlds.

equation.label: CENTRAL
equation.expression: U = (10000 / (169269 / (960/.28))) × .75 plan realization × .30 cash additionality × .80 unique fraction; QBay = U × [Σ(primary-needs share × unmet access × safe use × utility × finite years) − .00015 harm] × .95

inputs.label: Full annual cost boundary
inputs.basis: Actual full legal-entity expense is disclosed separately from the newer planning budget. No overhead is excluded.

inputs.label: Client-equivalent planning denominator
inputs.basis: Projected district clients divided by a reported historical district share. This is not an actual annual unique census. Central plan realization is 75%; unique fraction is 80%.

inputs.label: Cash additionality
inputs.basis: Accounts for other donors, public funding, reserves and operational capacity. Separate unmet-access factors address recipients' alternatives.

inputs.label: Exclusive dominant-need shares
inputs.basis: Adult mobility, bathing/transfer, pediatric adaptive equipment and consumables. Shares are unmeasured and mutually exclusive; no device stacking.

inputs.label: Utility and finite years
inputs.range: Zero clinical effect in null/harm; maximum duration .75 year
inputs.basis: No clinical study supplies these coefficients for MELP. Years means incremental useful health-improving time before alternative access, need resolution, discontinuation or device failure ends the advantage—not the physical life of the equipment. The favorable pediatric .75-year horizon is an explicit extension assumption beyond AbleCloset’s usual six-month pediatric loan limit (extensions can be requested), not established pediatric evidence. No lifetime, developmental, mortality or caregiver credit is added.

inputs.label: Resident benefit allocation
inputs.basis: Historical county participation supports local presence, not current Bay/SF shares. PHCD share and opening hours are not residence allocation rules.

inputs.label: Joint scenario weights
inputs.range: Cash null / clinical null / harm / cautious / central / favorable
inputs.basis: Weights were locked before execution. The cautious world becomes net negative after independent harms and is retained.

sensitivity.case: Shared clinical priors: central scenario only
sensitivity.headline: MELP weighted $2,117,236; central $572,533
sensitivity.detail: Diagnostic replacement of adult mobility, bathing and supply utility/duration with ReCARES central values. Other factors and pediatric pathway are unchanged. Not a replacement forecast.

sensitivity.case: Shared clinical priors: all three benefit-pathway worlds
sensitivity.headline: MELP weighted $1,317,403; central $572,533
sensitivity.detail: Corresponding ReCARES utility/duration values replace only three matched categories in cautious, central and favorable worlds. Null/harm worlds, weights, costs, mix, additionality, geography and pediatric inputs remain unchanged.

sensitivity.headline: ReCARES weighted $507,197 with MELP matched clinical values
sensitivity.detail: Central-only reverse swap gives $250,711 weighted and $455,104 central. Swapping all three benefit-pathway worlds gives $507,197 weighted. Neither family is empirically established; these comparisons do not prove organizational superiority.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: The lower utility and duration assumptions used here are not established MELP-specific differences from ReCARES. Shared clinical-prior diagnostics materially change both estimates: MELP is $1.32 million per 10 Bay QALYs with matched ReCARES values, while the reverse swap raises ReCARES to $507,197. These are sensitivity checks, not preferred estimates or clinical calibration. With the base priors unchanged, removing and renormalizing away MELP's favorable world gives $35,395,501 per 10 Bay QALYs. The favorable world alone creates the 3% subjective mass below both thresholds; its $98,406 result is close to $100,000 and does not merit empirical precision.
model.fundingBoundary: No verified marginal offer. Historical cash of $193,488 is not current unrestricted cash. PHCD's $50,000 award in 2024–25 and Sequoia's $25,000 award in 2026–27 support a funded baseline; different periods are not summed. Complete societal resources are unknown.

evidence.result: $104,000 expenses, $193,488 cash/savings/investments and $195,635 net assets; no actual recipient count.
evidence.transfer: Not current unrestricted liquidity or donation marginality.

evidence.design: Public grant applications and official instructions
evidence.result: Real repair/loan operations; reported 3,874 items in a recent 12-month period; newer forecast 960 district clients.
evidence.transfer: Items, visits, people and forecasts are not interchangeable.

evidence.design: Controlled walking-aid trials and provision guidance
evidence.population: Older emergency-department patients and COPD patients, not MELP borrowers
evidence.result: Some functional benefit but null quality-of-life findings; safe use and fit matter.
evidence.transfer: No MELP utility coefficient identified; no QALY mapping invented.

reservations: Whole-gift result is poor under stated priors; do not call this a high-EV recommendation.
Cash reserves and public grants may finance existing operations without the donor.
The denominator is inferred from a planning target and historical district share; actual unique users remain unknown.
All utility, duration, mix, use and causal access assumptions are judgments.
No delivery; first-come availability may exclude those most constrained.
Favorable tail dominates expected benefit despite small prior weight.
Complete donated equipment, volunteer, public partner and recipient resource costs are unpriced.
excludedBenefits: Retail replacement value and recipient financial savings
Separate falls, mortality and hospitalization benefits on top of utility
